description: Mandibular morphology and chin (mental) anatomy: jaw width, mandibular angle, masseter prominence, chin shape and projection, submental contour. Dimensions are drawn from craniofacial anthropometry (Farkas), facial-aesthetics literature (González-Ulloa, Riedel), and orthognathic-surgery references. Mandibular morphology has substantial population-level variation; East Asian populations average wider bigonial breadth and more prominent masseter musculature than European populations.

dimensions.scale_citation: Farkas LG (1994). Anthropometry of the Head and Face, 2nd Edition. Reference: bigonial breadth (go-go) relative to bizygomatic breadth (zy-zy).
dimensions.description: Width of the lower jaw at the gonial angles (bigonial breadth) relative to the cheekbones (bizygomatic breadth).

values.definition: Bigonial breadth substantially less than bizygomatic; tapered lower face.
Bigonial breadth approximately 75-85% of bizygomatic; aesthetic reference range.
Bigonial breadth approaches or exceeds bizygomatic; squared or wider-than-cheekbones lower face. Common in East Asian populations.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with orthognathic-surgery descriptors of mandibular angle morphology; reference values approximately 120-130° for the angle between the mandibular ramus and body.

values.definition: Visible 90°-leaning angle at the gonial point; defined jawline. More common in male physiognomy and in East Asian populations.
Standard 120-130° angle; defined but rounded gonial transition.
Smooth, rounded transition with no distinct angle. More common in female physiognomy and with subcutaneous fat coverage.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in masseter-reduction (botulinum toxin / surgical) literature on the East Asian face.
dimensions.description: Prominence of the masseter muscle as a visible jaw-region landmark. Hypertrophic masseter is the basis for the 'square jaw' appearance distinct from skeletal jaw width.

values.definition: Masseter not visibly contributing to jaw silhouette.
Masseter visible at clench but not at rest.
Masseter visible as a distinct landmark even at rest; squared lower face.
Pronounced masseter mass; visible bulge at the lower jaw.

dimensions.scale_citation: Riedel RA (1957). An analysis of dentofacial relationships. American Journal of Orthodontics, 43(2). Reference: pogonion-to-vertical-line relationship as the standard for chin projection assessment.
dimensions.description: Anterior projection of the chin (pogonion) in lateral view.

values.definition: Pogonion sits posterior to the Riedel reference plane; receding chin.
Pogonion approximately at the Riedel reference plane.
Pogonion sits anterior to the reference plane; prominent chin.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in genioplasty literature.
dimensions.description: Shape of the chin in frontal view.

values.definition: V-shaped chin with narrow apex.
Smooth U-shape; no distinct point or angle.
Wide, flat chin with sharp lateral angles.
Visible vertical midline indentation in the chin pad.
Notable left-right chin asymmetry.

dimensions.scale_citation: Farkas LG (1994). Reference: chin height (subnasale to menton) proportional to lower facial third.
dimensions.description: Vertical chin height proportional to the lower facial third.

values.definition: Chin height less than lower facial third reference.
Chin height within the reference range.
Chin height substantially above reference.

dimensions.scale_citation: Ellenbogen R, Karlin JV (1980). Visual criteria for success in restoring the youthful neck. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 66(6): 826-837. The Ellenbogen-Karlin neck-aesthetics criteria include submental contour as a primary dimension.
dimensions.description: Visibility of the chin-to-neck transition; presence of submental fat or laxity ('double chin').

values.definition: Crisp transition between chin and neck; no submental fat.
Visible chin-neck transition with some submental fullness.
Visible submental fat pad obscuring the chin-neck angle.
Pronounced submental fat creating a second visible chin contour.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with the contemporary aesthetic-medicine literature on jawline definition (Sundaram et al., Aesthetic Surgery Journal).
dimensions.description: Visibility of the mandibular contour from gonial angle to chin.

values.definition: Clear mandibular silhouette visible from frontal and profile views; no submental fat coverage.
Mandibular contour visible but soft.
Mandibular contour partially obscured by soft-tissue coverage.
Mandibular contour not discernible; full soft-tissue coverage of the jawline.

references: Farkas LG (1994). Anthropometry of the Head and Face, 2nd Edition. Raven Press.
Riedel RA (1957). An analysis of dentofacial relationships. American Journal of Orthodontics, 43(2): 103-119.
Ellenbogen R, Karlin JV (1980). Visual criteria for success in restoring the youthful neck. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 66(6): 826-837.
González-Ulloa M (1968). Quantitative principles in cosmetic surgery of the face: profile-plasty. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 41(2).

Sundaram H, Liew S, Signorini M, et al. (2016). Global aesthetics consensus: hyaluronic acid fillers and botulinum toxin type A — recommendations for combined treatment and optimizing outcomes in diverse patient populations. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 137(5).
